result:
Round 222 is planned. Decision: **CONTINUE**. It fixes the only open Medium bug, B-R220-LEGACY-EXPORT-NO-STEMS: in the purchased Studio, the export dialog opens with 0 of 10 stems ticked, so "Export Audio" stays disabled until the user presses "Select All".

**Round 221 is closed.** C passed 13 rows and the browser checks ran (`browserVerified` and `realVerified` true). Gate 221 published `6dd45a1`, which is the baseline for round 222, and PERF-16 is now complete. Two rulings came with it:
- **C-R221-01 (Low):** closed. The check's real meaning was "no installed `@ffmpeg` package", and C measured exactly that. The empty `node_modules/@ffmpeg/` folder is left over from root's uninstall and isn't tracked in git.
- **Gate-221 review:** three of its findings moved to the deferred Low list, which went from 341 to 345 with a fourth new Low. The two others were already open: the stale `vite.config.ts` entry (with root) and the outdated ffmpeg guidance in agent files (waiting for Saba).

**The fix.** The dialog is created before the product's stems load, so its "all selected" starting value captures an empty list. The new rule:
- When the set of stem IDs changes (first load, another product), every current stem is selected.
- Mute, solo or volume changes keep the user's ticks, and so do closing and reopening the dialog. These matter because `StudioContext` rebuilds the stem list on each of them with the same IDs.

**Files.**
- `app/components/studio/ExportDialog.tsx`: a narrow grant, covering the selection logic only.
- New test `app/lib/__tests__/legacy-export-dialog-stems.test.tsx`, with seven checks (ES1–ES7).
- New doc 174.
- The protected purchase route and the frozen `StudioContext.tsx` are not touched.

I tried a seven-line fix in a scratch copy, not in the repo. The new tests fail on the current code and pass with that fix, and the type check is clean.

**What C checks in the browser.**
- The dialog opens at 10/10 with "Export Audio" enabled, at 1440×900 and 1280×720. A WAV exported without touching the selection matches one exported after Deselect All → Select All, in the same session.
- With one stem unticked, that stem's tone is missing from the exported audio. C records which stem had which tone.
- Unticking a stem survives closing and reopening, and survives muting a different stem.
- The sign-in guard is checked without any fake responses. The real ownership check stays blocked because there is no backend in the cloud.

**Ableton reference.** The Live 12 manual (§5.1.3.1) lists the export options and says most users pick "Main" (the full mix). It never says what the default is or whether settings are remembered, so the task records both as unconfirmed and claims neither. Being able to choose stems inside the dialog is recorded as better than Live, which only renders tracks selected before the dialog opens.

**Other notes.**
- I wrote `b-round-221-checkpoint-request.md`, asking root for an architecture review of the export pipeline. It does not block anything.
- No project subagents were consulted. The advisor was used twice and all its points were adopted; the main one is that the trigger is the set of stem IDs.
- The regression round isn't due until 2026-10-30. If round 222 passes before then, round 223 is PERF-HARNESS-SHARED-LIB.
- The store repo is untouched and its tree is clean.
- **For Saba:** may the loop update the agent and rule files that still teach the removed ffmpeg package, or will you? Agents aren't allowed to edit them, and the gate reviewer rates the issue Medium for agent tooling.
